Hi Oliver — looping in technical details and a recommended migration approach so your infra/security teams have something concrete to review. Attaching a migration checklist (medlytix-migration-checklist.xlsx) with a rough task split.

Short answers to your migration questions and recommended path:
- Model artifacts: our Dedicated and Private runtimes support standard PyTorch weights and common transformer formats. We often help customers with a short conversion step for optimized kernels (3–7 days of engineering work for a mid-sized model), plus extra time for quantization if desired.
- Bring-your-own-weights: supported in Private deployments and in some Dedicated configurations (we can discuss EULA/hosting terms). If you must keep weights on-prem, our Private on-prem package can be installed behind your firewall — that’s the lowest-friction for full data residency.
- Connectivity: given the "no public egress" constraint, options are (ranked):
  1) Private on-prem deployment (package installed in your DC) — no egress, full control.
  2) VPC Peering / AWS PrivateLink to Redwood Dedicated in your region — keeps data on private network paths and enables Redwood-managed infra.
  3) Dedicated-hosted with encrypted outbound to a customer-controlled endpoint — only if policy allows limited egress.

Staged migration we recommend:
1) Validate: small proof-of-concept in parallel against a subset of requests (can run on Hosted sandbox or a short-lived Dedicated cluster).
2) Dual-run: route a % of traffic to Redwood (mirroring) to validate behavior and latency.
3) Canary: controlled cutover for a single region or subset of users; monitor for regressions.
4) Cutover & decommission: once thresholds met, switch traffic and decommission legacy stack.

Risks and mitigations:
- Latency tuning: need kernel selection and batch sizing adjustments — we’ll profile once we have traces.
- KV cache warm-up: initial cold-starts can be noisy; we recommend warming with synthetic load during canary.
- Model quality drift: run evals with your labeled prompts during validation.

Next steps I propose:
- Share SOC2 summary and network diagram (Nikhil will attach).
- 30-min technical sync (I can walk the infra team through Private vs PrivateLink steps).
- We’ll fill the migration checklist with estimated durations and owners.

Proposed times: Fri 09:30–10:00 PT or Mon 11:00–11:30 PT — shout which works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
